sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, school bus signals, right of way and passing

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Yellow hazard lights on a bus mean caution, yellow overhead lights mean prepare to stop, and only red overhead lights require you to stop 20 feet back. [A01]
Why it matters: group school bus; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec07-F02, sec07-F03, sec07-F04 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A02
At a four-way stop the first to stop goes first, and only on a tie does the driver on the left yield to the driver on the right. [A02]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec07-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A02
A malfunctioning signal is treated like a stop: stop fully, let vehicles already there go, and on a tie yield to the right. [A02]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec07-F13, sec07-F14 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn but only after yielding, while a flashing red signal requires a complete stop first. [A02]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec07-F12, sec07-F15 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A02
A green light does not give you the right of way over vehicles still clearing the intersection or over oncoming traffic when you turn left. [A02]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec07-F10, sec07-F11 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A02
At a T-intersection without signs, the driver on the ending road yields to traffic on the through road. [A02]
Why it matters: group intersections; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec07-F16 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A04
After passing, you must be back in your lane before you are within 200 feet of oncoming traffic, while the no-passing distance near intersections and railroad crossings is 100 feet. [A04]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec07-F32, sec07-F39 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A04
Passing on the right is legal in the listed cases, but using the shoulder or leaving the pavement to do it never is. [A04]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec07-F36, sec07-F37 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A04
The center lane of a three-lane road may be used to pass unless it is marked for left turns only, in which case passing and merging there are banned. [A04]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec07-F34, sec07-F40 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A03
Funeral processions outrank all traffic except fire, ambulance and police vehicles, yet you are not required to pull over for one; you only must not cut through it. [A03]
Why it matters: group special right of way; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec07-F27, sec07-F29 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A03
A green light never overrides a pedestrian already in the crosswalk. [A03]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec07-F21, sec07-F26 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0045]
